title: Sections 2 and 3: assessment and treatment
blurb: Choose between s2 and s3, state their criteria and time limits, and explain the nearest relative's role.
question: Ana, 29, has had three admissions for bipolar disorder with a well-established treatment plan. She has stopped her medication, is acutely manic and refuses admission. The AMHP and two doctors agree she needs detention. Which section is most appropriate and why?

teach.body: Section 2 is admission for assessment (or assessment followed by treatment) for up to 28 days. Section 3 is admission for treatment for up to 6 months, renewable. Both need an application by an AMHP or the nearest relative, founded on two medical recommendations. In plain English: s2 is 'we need to find out what is going on'; s3 is 'we know what is going on and the person needs treatment in hospital'.

teach.caption: Both sections allow treatment for mental disorder under s63, subject to the Part 4 safeguards.

head: Section
All of these must apply
rows: Mental disorder of a nature or degree warranting detention for assessment for at least a limited period
Ought to be detained for own health or safety or protection of others
Mental disorder of a nature or degree making hospital treatment appropriate
Necessary for health, safety or protection of others, and cannot be given unless detained

children.label: Section 3
children.sub: A new s2 cannot renew s2

teach.caption: The reasons for choosing s2 or s3 should be clearly recorded (COP15 14.29).

teach.h: Scenario: Ana on the admissions ward
teach.body: Ana's diagnosis, the essential treatment plan and her likely response are already well established from three previous admissions, so a fresh assessment is not needed: s3 is the right route (COP15 14.28). The AMHP must consult her mother, who is her nearest relative, and cannot apply if her mother objects. On the ward, Ana's nurse gives her s132 rights, including her right to apply to the tribunal once in the first 6 months.

teach.text: Section 2 cannot be renewed and cannot be followed by another s2. If a person on s2 needs to stay, the route is s3. Also: the nearest relative can BLOCK an AMHP's s3 application by objecting, but has no power to block s2 (only to be told and to seek discharge).

items: s2: assessment, up to 28 days, not renewable; NR informed.
s3: treatment, up to 6 months, renewable for 6 months then yearly; NR consulted and can object.
Both: AMHP (or NR) applies with two medical recommendations, one from a s12 approved doctor.
Use s3 when the disorder and treatment plan are established, or the person is already on s2.

summary: You can now choose between s2 and s3 using the Code's criteria, state their time limits and grounds, and explain how two medical recommendations and the AMHP's application fit together. You can also describe the different roles of the nearest relative under each section.

A.q: What is the maximum length of detention under section 2 of the Mental Health Act 1983?
A.why: Section 2(4): a patient may be detained for a period not exceeding 28 days beginning with the day of admission.

whyNot.0: 72 hours is the limit for s4 emergency admission and the s5(2) holding power.
whyNot.1: 14 days is the window for a s2 patient to apply to the tribunal.
whyNot.3: 6 months is the first period of detention under s3.

A.q: A patient's section 3 is renewed for the first time. For how long does the first renewal last?
A.why: Under s20, s3 lasts up to 6 months, may be renewed for a further 6 months, and then for 1 year at a time.

whyNot.0: Three-month periods are a 2025 Act change that is not in force.
whyNot.1: Yearly renewals begin after the first 6-month renewal.
whyNot.2: 28 days is the s2 limit, which cannot be renewed.

A.q: How many medical recommendations does an application under section 3 require?
A.why: Section 3(3): an application for admission for treatment is founded on the written recommendations of two registered medical practitioners.

whyNot.1: One recommendation is enough only for an emergency s4 application.
whyNot.2: The Act requires two medical recommendations, not three.
whyNot.3: The AMHP is the applicant; the application still needs two medical recommendations.

B.q: Mr Evans is detained under section 2. On day 24 the team agree he needs further treatment in hospital and he still refuses to stay. What is the appropriate legal route?
options: Renewal of the section 2 by the RC
B.why: COP15 14.28: s3 should be used if the patient is already detained under s2, because s2 cannot be renewed by a new s2 application.

whyNot.0: A new s2 cannot be used to extend an existing s2.
whyNot.3: Section 5(2) applies to informal in-patients, not to someone already detained.

B.q: An AMHP is considering a section 3 application for Ms Clarke. Her husband, who is her nearest relative, says he objects. What is the effect?
options: The AMHP may apply after recording the objection
The objection matters for a section 2 instead
The AMHP cannot make the section 3 application
The RC may override the objection in writing
B.why: Section 11(4)(a): an AMHP may not make a s3 application if the nearest relative has notified an objection.

whyNot.0: Recording the objection does not remove the statutory bar.
whyNot.1: For s2 the AMHP informs the nearest relative; there is no power to block s2 by objection.
whyNot.3: The RC has no power to override an objection to an application; displacement is for the county court.

B.q: Which feature applies to section 3 but NOT to section 2?
options: The AMHP or nearest relative can apply
Appropriate medical treatment must be available
Treatment can be given without consent under section 63
B.why: The appropriate medical treatment test is in s3(2)(d); s2 has no such test.

whyNot.0: Both sections need two medical recommendations.
whyNot.1: Both applications may be made by an AMHP or the nearest relative.
whyNot.3: Patients on either section can be treated under s63, subject to Part 4 safeguards.

C.q: Jamal, 19, is brought to the assessment suite with a first episode of unusual beliefs and withdrawal. No diagnosis has been made and he will not stay voluntarily. Two doctors and an AMHP agree that detention is needed. Which section best fits the Code?
options: Section 3, to allow treatment to begin
Section 2, because the picture is unclear
Section 4, as it is a first presentation
C.why: COP15 14.27: s2 is used where the full extent of the nature and degree of the condition is unclear or an initial in-patient assessment is needed.

whyNot.0: Section 3 fits where the disorder and treatment plan are already established.
whyNot.2: Section 4 is for urgent necessity where waiting for a second doctor would cause undesirable delay.
whyNot.3: Section 5(2) applies to someone who is already an in-patient, not a new admission.

C.q: Two doctors examine Mrs Ito separately for a section 2 application. What is the legal limit on the gap between their examinations?
C.why: Section 12(1): where doctors examine the patient separately, not more than five days may elapse between the examinations.

whyNot.1: 24 hours relates to s4 (the applicant must have seen the person within 24 hours) and to place-of-safety detention.
whyNot.2: 14 days is the period within which the applicant must have personally seen the patient (s11(5)).
whyNot.3: 72 hours is the s4 and s5(2) time limit.

C.q: Ana is detained under section 3. Her nurse is explaining her rights. Which statement is accurate?
options: She can apply to the tribunal within the first 14 days
She can apply to the tribunal once in the first 6 months
Her mother can end the section at any time by writing to managers
C.why: Section 66(2): a s3 patient may apply to the tribunal once in the first 6 months, then once in each renewal period.

whyNot.0: The 14-day window applies to s2 patients.
whyNot.1: Section 3 lasts up to 6 months; 28 days is s2.
whyNot.3: The nearest relative can order discharge with 72 hours' notice, but the RC can bar it on dangerousness grounds.

reteach.title: Find out or fix
reteach.question: If you only remembered one idea about s2 and s3, what should it be?

blocks.body: Section 2 is for FINDING OUT: the picture is unclear or needs a fresh in-patient assessment, so the law allows up to 28 days. Section 3 is for FIXING: the disorder and plan are known and the person needs treatment in hospital, so the law allows 6 months with renewals, but adds safeguards: the nearest relative can object, appropriate treatment must be available and after-care under s117 follows.

items.label: s3 first period and first renewal

blocks.text: The nearest relative's objection blocks an AMHP's s3 application, not a s2 application.

explain.body: Admission for assessment, or assessment followed by treatment, for up to 28 days from admission. It cannot be renewed. The AMHP informs the nearest relative, who can later order discharge.

test.q: Which statement about section 2 is correct?
options: It can be renewed once for 28 days
It lasts up to 28 days from admission
The nearest relative's objection blocks it
It needs appropriate treatment to be available
test.why: Section 2(4) limits detention to 28 days from the day of admission.

whyNot.0: Section 2 has no renewal; s3 is used if detention must continue.
whyNot.2: An objection blocks s3, not s2.

explain.body: Admission for treatment for up to 6 months, renewable for 6 months then yearly. Grounds include that treatment cannot be given unless detained and that appropriate medical treatment is available.

test.q: Which is one of the statutory grounds for section 3?
options: Treatment cannot be given unless detained
The diagnosis is not yet established
Waiting for a second doctor causes delay
The person is already an informal in-patient
test.why: Section 3(2)(c) requires that treatment is necessary and cannot be provided unless the person is detained.

whyNot.1: An unclear diagnosis points to s2.
whyNot.2: Undesirable delay is the s4 emergency test.
whyNot.3: Being an informal in-patient is relevant to s5 holding powers.

explain.body: Two doctors recommend. One must be approved under s12 as having special experience in mental disorder; the other should, if practicable, know the person. Separate examinations must be no more than 5 days apart.

test.q: Which requirement applies to the two medical recommendations under Part 2?
options: Both doctors must be consultant psychiatrists
One doctor must be approved under section 12
One doctor must be the patient's RC
test.why: Section 12(2): one recommendation must come from a practitioner approved as having special experience in mental disorder.

whyNot.0: The Act requires one s12 approved doctor, not two consultants.
whyNot.2: There is no requirement that the RC gives a recommendation.
whyNot.3: They may examine together or separately, up to 5 days apart.

explain.body: For s2 the AMHP takes practicable steps to inform the nearest relative. For s3 the AMHP must consult them (unless not reasonably practicable or causing unreasonable delay) and cannot apply if they object.

test.q: When must an AMHP consult the nearest relative before applying, unless impracticable or causing unreasonable delay?
test.why: Section 11(4)(b) requires consultation with the nearest relative before an AMHP's s3 application.

whyNot.0: For s2 the duty is to inform the nearest relative, not consult.
whyNot.1: Section 5(4) is a nurse's emergency holding power with no AMHP application.
whyNot.2: Section 136 is a police power, not an AMHP application.
